text: Deadlines are a part of professional life, and handling them well requires more than just hard work. Good time management is the foundation, meaning you break large tasks into smaller, manageable steps with their own mini-deadlines. This prevents last-minute panic. Prioritization is equally important; you must decide which tasks are truly urgent and which can wait, focusing your energy where it matters most. Equally, you need to practice scope management, politely saying no to extra requests that could derail your original plan. Finally, never underestimate the power of communication. If you sense a deadline is unrealistic, tell your manager or client early, offering a revised timeline. This builds trust far more than silently struggling and missing the date.
